matches.title: Brighton vs Wolverhampton
matches.description: Watch Brighton vs Wolverhampton highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 9, 2026. The atmosphere at the Amex Stadium was electric for this Premier League clash on May 9, 2026 . With both sides eager to establish dominance, the match began as a tactical puzzle waiting to be solved under the afternoon sun. A Lightning Start for the Seagulls Brighton produced a masterclass in early efficiency, stunning Wolverhampton with two goals in the opening five minutes. The deadlock was broken in the very first minute when Kaoru Mitoma initiated a move that saw Maxim De Cuyper deliver a pinpoint cross for Jack Hinshelwood to head home. Before the visitors could catch their breath, the lead was doubled in the 5th minute. Another superb delivery from a De Cuyper corner found captain Lewis Dunk , who rose highest to power a header past Daniel Bentley . This early blitz allowed Brighton to dictate the tempo, maintaining a staggering 73% of ball possession throughout the contest. Wolverhampton struggled to find an answer to the Seagulls' fluid movement, with Daniel Bentley forced into several saves to deny Danny Welbeck from adding a third before the break. Tactical Battle and Rising Tension The match grew increasingly physical as Wolverhampton tried to claw their way back into contention. Yellow cards were shown to Hee-Chan Hwang and Andre for dangerous challenges, while Kaoru Mitoma also found his way into the referee's book. Despite the tactical substitutions made by the Wolves' bench, including the introduction of Tolu Arokodare and Angel Gomes , the hosts remained disciplined in their defensive shape. Brighton 's dominance was not just in possession but also in territory, as they forced numerous corners and kept the pressure high. The visitors' frustration was evident as multiple offside calls against Hee-Chan Hwang and Hugo Bueno neutralized their sporadic counter-attacking threats. Minteh Puts the Game to Bed As the clock ticked towards the final whistle, Brighton ensured there would be no late drama. In the 86th minute, Yankuba Minteh found space and unleashed a clinical left-footed strike that nestled into the back of the net, effectively sealing the three points. The goal was a just reward for a side that had controlled the narrative from the opening whistle. In the closing moments, Wolverhampton had a brief chance through Tolu Arokodare , but his header flashed wide of the target. With 31,587 fans in attendance, the referee blew the final whistle to confirm a deserved and emphatic victory for the Seagulls, who showcased both flair and defensive solidity to see out the game.

matches.title: Wolverhampton vs Sunderland
matches.description: Watch Wolverhampton vs Sunderland highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 2, 2026. Molineux played host to a high-stakes Premier League encounter as Wolverhampton and Sunderland faced off in a match defined by tactical discipline and sudden shifts in momentum. The atmosphere was electric on May 2, 2026 , as both sides looked to seize control of a contest that promised drama from the opening whistle. Early Breakthrough and Defensive Discipline The visitors found their rhythm early in the match, making their intentions clear through set-piece efficiency. In the 17th minute, Sunderland silenced the home crowd when Granit Xhaka delivered a pinpoint corner from the right flank. Nordi Mukiele rose highest in the box, connecting with a powerful header that flew past the goalkeeper to give the Black Cats an early lead. The goal rewarded the visitors' clinical start, but the game took a drastic turn just seven minutes later. In the 24th minute, the match official was forced to reach for his back pocket following a serious foul by Daniel Ballard . The referee showed no hesitation in brandishing a straight red card, dismissing the defender and leaving Sunderland to play more than an hour of football with only ten men. Despite the numerical disadvantage, the visitors retreated into a compact defensive shape, with goalkeeper Robin Roefs proving a formidable barrier. Tolu Arokodare spearheaded the Wolverhampton response, seeing several headed efforts saved by Roefs as the first half drew to a close with the scoreline still favoring the away side. The Bueno Connection and VAR Tension Wolverhampton returned for the second half with renewed vigor, immediately pinning the ten-man visitors back into their own territory. The pressure finally told in the 54th minute through a moment of familial-named synchronicity. Hugo Bueno swung a high-quality corner into the danger zone, where Santiago Bueno was waiting to meet it. The defender’s header found the back of the net, but the celebrations were momentarily halted as the referee initiated a VAR check. After a tense review, the goal was confirmed, drawing the hosts level and leaving Granit Xhaka so incensed he received a yellow card for dissent. Seeking a winner, the Wolverhampton bench introduced Rodrigo Gomes and Angel Gomes to inject more creativity into the final third. The hosts dominated the ball, maintaining 58% possession throughout the contest, but they found it increasingly difficult to break through a resilient Sunderland block. Adam Armstrong saw an effort ruled out for offside, while Arokodare continued to test the defense, only to see his best efforts blocked by the determined backline. A Frantic Finish at Molineux As the clock ticked toward the 90th minute, the tension among the 29,632 fans in attendance reached a fever pitch. Sunderland ’s defensive effort became increasingly desperate, leading to a flurry of bookings as Dennis Cirkin and Robin Roefs both entered the referee's book for fouls and dissent respectively. Despite the pressure, the visitors nearly snatched a late winner against the run of play in stoppage time when Nordi Mukiele forced a sharp save from the Wolves keeper following a cross from Trai Hume . In the final moments, Wolverhampton threw everything forward, with Tolu Arokodare sending a late effort wide of the target after being set up by Adam Armstrong . However, the ten men of Sunderland held firm through three minutes of added time, securing a gritty point on the road. The final whistle brought an end to a pulsating encounter where both sides could take pride in their resilience, even if the winning goal remained elusive.

matches.description: Watch Wolverhampton vs Fulham highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 17, 2026. Wolverhampton and Fulham locked horns on May 17, 2026 , in a Premier League fixture that promised high intensity and tactical intrigue. Both sets of fans filled the stadium expecting a battle that could define their respective seasons. First Half Fireworks Wolverhampton managed to break the deadlock in the 25th minute through a moment of individual brilliance. Hee-Chan Hwang provided the crucial assist, finding Mateus Mane outside the box. The young attacker unleashed a powerful right-footed shot that flew past the goalkeeper, giving the home side a hard-earned lead. Despite falling behind, Fulham remained composed, maintaining a staggering 70% of ball possession and dictating the tempo as they searched for a way back into the contest. Penalty Drama and VAR Intervention The momentum shifted dramatically just before the halftime whistle. Mateus Mane went from hero to villain when he conceded a penalty for dangerous play against Timothy Castagne . Following a tense VAR review, the referee pointed to the spot. In the 3rd minute of stoppage time, Antonee Robinson stepped up for Fulham and coolly converted the penalty with his left foot, sending Jose Sa the wrong way to level the scores. Woodwork and Late Pressure The second half was defined by missed opportunities and defensive resilience. Adam Armstrong came agonizingly close to restoring the lead for the hosts in the 68th minute, but his finish rattled the post. Managers on both sides introduced fresh legs, with Raul Jimenez and Harry Wilson entering the fray for Fulham , while Pedro Lima replaced Rodrigo Gomes for the hosts. In the dying moments, André received a yellow card for a foul on Joshua King , as Wolverhampton held firm against late Fulham pressure to ensure the spoils were shared.
